title: Unauthenticated visit to a protected route lands on the sign-in page in a browser (e2e)
asA: operator relying on the auth-surface discipline the application-spa blueprint declares
iWant: an end-to-end test that a real browser making an unauthenticated request against a protected route in the shipped application lands on the sign-in page rather than the protected surface
soThat: the arrival-and-auth discipline (application-spa-REQ-009: landing, sign-in, sign-out, expiry, recovery, onboarding, deep-link redirects) is verified end-to-end at a user-observable surface. Verify's auth-smoke pass is adversarial and complementary; this e2e case is the coverage anchor.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An unauthenticated visit to a protected route lands on the sign-in page in a browser. Verification navigates a real browser (fresh context, no persisted session, no injected cookies) to a protected route the blueprint declares under browserSurface.routes, and asserts the browser's final URL path is the sign-in route rather than the protected route. The check drives the same server construction the production entry point boots (no header-stripping harness, no app.inject substitute). A landing path equal to the requested route, or to any other page, refuses ship with a diagnostic naming the requested, landed and expected sign-in paths.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the application booted through its production entry point with a protected route and a sign-in route both registered
acceptanceCriteria.when: a real browser with no session state navigates to the protected route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the browser's final URL path equals the sign-in route path; any other landing (protected route rendered without auth, arbitrary other page, error page) refuses ship with a diagnostic naming requested, landed and expected paths

acceptanceCriteria.description: A signed-in browser opening a protected deep-link with a live session lands on the requested protected route, not on the sign-in route. A signed-in browser opening a sign-out surface and then reopening the same protected deep-link lands on the sign-in route with the originally requested route preserved on the return-to state named on TAC-201-application-spa-app-shell.responsibilities[0], and after a fresh sign-in the browser lands on the originally requested protected route. Applying agent sets: the project-declared browserSurface.routes for the protected route, the sign-in route, and the sign-out surface.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the application booted through its production entry point with a protected route, a sign-in route, and a sign-out surface all registered under browserSurface.routes
acceptanceCriteria.when: a signed-in browser opens the protected deep-link, then signs out, then reopens the same deep-link, then signs in again
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first open lands on the protected route; the second open (post sign-out) lands on the sign-in route with the return-to state preserving the originally requested path; the post-authentication landing is the originally requested protected route; any other landing refuses ship with a diagnostic naming the requested, landed, and expected paths

description: A boundary-path AC covering the deep-link preservation and post-sign-out return-to flow named on the app-shell; the arrival AC binds the unauthenticated-redirect success signal, this AC binds the signed-in and post-sign-out boundary transitions.
